page: Microsoft Azure F32ams_v6 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the Famsv6 family. It features 32 dedicated physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The hardware configuration allocates 1.0 thread per core, ensuring dedicated CPU resources without hyperthreading. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The processor includes 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache, alongside support for advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16) and cryptography standards like AES and SHA_NI.

Benchmark evaluations place the F32ams_v6 in the strong performance tier across multiple domains. In multi-core CPU testing via Geekbench, the server achieves a top-tier score of 21,894.0, placing it in the top 10% of tested systems. Image processing and small-model LLM prompt processing (135M model at 4,660.22 tokens/sec) also reach top-tier levels. Memory performance is robust, with cached small-block read bandwidth reaching 4,748.97 GB/sec and large-block write bandwidth at 109.68 GB/sec, both in the top 25%. However, uncached large-block read bandwidth drops to an average tier of 151.67 GB/sec.

This server does not include local storage, requiring external Premium Storage attachments for persistent disk operations. It also lacks integrated GPU hardware, which limits its utility for heavy graphical rendering or large-scale deep learning training, though it maintains strong CPU-based inference speeds for smaller language models. Given its high memory density of 256.0 GB and dedicated 32-core AMD EPYC processor, the F32ams_v6 is suited for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, software compilation, and multi-threaded data processing tasks.
